outline.description: This chapter introduces the underlying dispute, the specific factual circumstances surrounding Foad Farahi and the FBI, and the procedural history that led to the appellate review. It ensures students understand the scope of the request and the district court's initial difficulties before the final ruling.
subtopics: Foad Farahi's Immigration and FBI Profile
The Nature of the FOIA Request (Volume and Scope)
Litigation Timeline and District Court Deadlines
Initial Summary Judgment Motion by the FBI
First Amendment/Adjudication (Substitutionary) Order and the Update Requirement
Renewed Motion and Final District Court Judgment
Grounds for Appeal on Foad Farahi's Part

outline.chapter_title: Legislative and Judicial Framework for FOIA Exemption 7(A)
outline.description: This chapter provides the doctrinal and statutory foundations required to understand the exemption at issue. It explains why the government bears the burden of proof and how the court applies standards of review to FOIA cases, specifically regarding the deference afforded to law enforcement agencies.
subtopics: The Freedom of Information Act's General Mandate
The Specifics of Exemption 7(A) Statutory Language
Burden of Proof on the Government
Standard of Review for Summary Judgment (De Novo)
Deference to Agency Determinations in National Security/Enforcement Cases
Requirement for Reasonable Segregation of Nonexempt Information

outline.description: This chapter applies the legal standards from Chapter 2 to the specific facts of the case. It details how the court evaluated the FBI's declarations to determine if the records were compiled for law enforcement and if their release would interfere with ongoing investigations.
subtopics: Establishing a 'Law Enforcement Purpose' Nexus
Determining 'Pending or Reasonably Anticipated' Proceedings
The 'Tipping Off' Theory of Interference
Rethinking the Passage of Time (Staleness Argument)
Sufficiency of Government Affidavits (Hardy and Bender Declarations)
Contextual Evidence: Terrorist Connections and Ongoing Investigations

outline.chapter_title: Segregation Duties and Review of Ex Parte Materials
outline.description: This final chapter addresses the technical requirements of record release. It explores the obligation to release nonexempt portions when possible and evaluates the procedural propriety of the district court relying on ex parte submissions to make its fact-finding.
subtopics: The Obligation to Release 'Reasonably Segregable' Material
The 'Inextricably Intertwined' Standard for Full Withholding
Line-by-Line vs. Meaningful Information Segregation
Procedural Acceptance of Ex Parte Declarations
Forfeiture of Segregability Challenges (Farahi's Silence)
Final Disposition and Affirmance of the District Court
